questions.scenario: Place the stages of a typical AI/ML lifecycle in the correct order, from first to last.
questions.explain: Data always comes first — a model can only learn from what you give it. Training follows, then evaluation against held-out data, then deployment, then ongoing monitoring which may trigger retraining. AWS gives no partial credit on ordering questions, so this sequence must be exact.

questions.scenario: Order these foundation model customisation approaches from LOWEST cost to HIGHEST cost.
questions.explain: Prompt engineering costs nothing beyond tokens. RAG adds retrieval infrastructure but leaves the model untouched. Fine-tuning requires training compute. Pre-training from scratch costs millions and is almost never the exam's answer. Work down this list only as far as you must.

questions.scenario: Order the steps of a Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) request, from first to last.
options: The user's question is converted into an embedding
Similar document chunks are retrieved from the vector store
The retrieved chunks are added to the prompt as context
The foundation model generates an answer grounded in that context
questions.explain: RAG works by turning the question into a vector, finding semantically similar chunks, injecting them into the prompt, and only then generating. Understanding this order is what makes it obvious why RAG reflects updated documents immediately — the retrieval happens fresh on every request.

questions.scenario: Order these steps for responsibly investigating a report that a deployed model is producing biased outputs, from first to last.
options: Measure bias across demographic subgroups with SageMaker Clarify
Examine the training data for representation gaps
Retrain and re-evaluate the model before redeploying
questions.explain: Measure before you act: confirm and quantify the bias first, then trace it to its usual source in the training data, then fix the data, then retrain and verify. Jumping straight to retraining without measuring means you cannot tell whether anything improved.

questions.scenario: Match each AWS service to the task it performs.
options: Analyses text for sentiment and entities
Identifies objects and faces in images
questions.explain: Transcribe = speech to text. Comprehend = understanding text (sentiment, entities, PII). Rekognition = images and video. Polly = text to speech. Remember Polly as the parrot that speaks, and Transcribe as writing down what was said.

questions.scenario: Match each responsible-AI need to the AWS capability that addresses it.
options: Detects bias and explains individual predictions
Blocks harmful content and denied topics
Routes low-confidence predictions to human reviewers
Documents a model's intended use and limitations
questions.explain: Clarify = fairness and explainability. Guardrails = content safety in Bedrock. A2I = human-in-the-loop review. Model Cards = transparency documentation. The pair most often confused is Guardrails (stops it speaking) versus Clarify (explains why it spoke).

questions.scenario: Match each prompting technique to its description.
options: No examples are provided, only the instruction
The model is asked to reason step by step
questions.explain: Zero-shot gives no examples, one-shot gives exactly one, few-shot gives several, and chain-of-thought requests intermediate reasoning. The 'shot' count refers to examples; chain-of-thought is about reasoning, which is why it helps most on multi-step arithmetic and logic.

questions.scenario: Match each learning approach to the kind of data it requires.
options: Labelled examples showing the correct answer
Unlabelled data, where the model finds structure itself
Feedback in the form of rewards and penalties
questions.explain: Supervised learning needs labels, unsupervised learning finds patterns without them, and reinforcement learning learns from rewards. Labels are the dividing line and are usually the most expensive part of an ML project.

questions.scenario: Match each security concern to the control that addresses it.
options: Users hiding instructions in input to hijack the model
Confidential data appearing in model responses
Discovering personal data stored in Amazon S3
Recording who called which API and when
questions.explain: Prompt injection is countered by input validation and output filtering. Data leakage is countered by Guardrails masking PII. Macie discovers sensitive data in S3. CloudTrail provides the audit trail. Prompt injection is the AI equivalent of SQL injection — never trust user input as instructions.

questions.scenario: Match each evaluation metric to what it measures.
options: Of all genuine positive cases, how many were caught
Of all flagged cases, how many were genuine
questions.explain: ROUGE = summarisation, BLEU = translation, recall = how many real cases you caught, precision = how many of your flags were right. Recall matters when missing a case is dangerous (disease, fraud); precision matters when false alarms are costly (spam filters).

questions.scenario: A company's support assistant must answer from documentation that is updated weekly and cite the source document. Which approach is correct?
questions.explain: Weekly updates plus a citation requirement both point to RAG, which reads live documents at query time and can reference them. Fine-tuning absorbs knowledge into weights, cannot cite sources, and would need repeating every week.

questions.scenario: Which statement about tokens is correct?
options: A token is roughly three-quarters of a word, and you are billed for both input and output tokens
Tokens are only counted during training
A token is always exactly one word
Tokens apply only to image models
questions.explain: Tokens are the units models read and generate — roughly three-quarters of a word — and both the prompt and the response are billed. This is why concise prompts and capped output lengths reduce cost.

questions.scenario: A company wants to group customers by purchasing behaviour without any predefined categories. Which approach?
questions.explain: No predefined categories means no labels, which is unsupervised learning — clustering finds the groupings itself. Supervised classification would require labelled examples of each category up front.

questions.scenario: A model performs excellently on its training data but poorly on new data. What is this called?
questions.explain: Overfitting means the model memorised the training data rather than learning generalisable patterns. Underfitting is the opposite — it learned too little and performs poorly everywhere. Drift is degradation over time after deployment.

questions.scenario: Which practice best prevents confidential information from appearing in a chatbot's responses?
options: Bedrock Guardrails with PII masking plus output filtering
questions.explain: Guardrails can detect and mask PII, and output filtering validates responses before delivery. Temperature and context window do not affect data leakage, and disabling logging would remove the audit trail you need.

questions.scenario: Which AWS service provides serverless API access to foundation models from multiple providers?
questions.explain: Bedrock gives serverless API access to foundation models with no infrastructure to manage. SageMaker AI is for building and training your own models, which requires far more expertise.

questions.scenario: An application needs consistent, repeatable answers to factual questions. Which inference setting?
questions.explain: Low temperature reduces randomness, producing consistent output suited to factual and numerical work. High temperature increases creative variation, which is the opposite of what factual answering needs.

questions.scenario: Under the shared responsibility model, which is the customer's responsibility when using Amazon Bedrock?
options: The data and prompts they supply, and IAM access control
questions.explain: Your data, your prompts and your access control are always yours. AWS secures the infrastructure, the service and the model itself. The rule is unchanged on AI services: what you cannot touch belongs to AWS.

questions.scenario: Which pair of AWS capabilities together support explaining and documenting a high-risk model?
options: SageMaker Clarify and SageMaker Model Cards
questions.explain: Clarify explains why individual predictions occurred and measures bias; Model Cards document the model's intended use, data and limitations. Together they cover explainability and transparency, which regulators typically require.

questions.scenario: Which AWS service would extract text and data from scanned invoices?
questions.explain: Textract extracts text, forms and tables from scanned documents — 'text' plus 'extract'. Comprehend analyses the meaning of text that already exists, and Rekognition analyses images rather than reading documents.
